LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 LISTENING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information, part of Strand 6 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: What is the importance of prepositions in description? 2. Why should we take care of animals?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work in partnership with peers to identify types of animals from audio recordings,

2. compose sentences describing the position of an object in relation to another with words such as next to, under, in front of, between, behind, on, in, beside, outside,

3. role play placing objects at different positions according to instructions given,

4. work closely with peers to identify prepositions from the passages,

5. answer comprehension questions,

6. listen to a resource person on imaginative stories on animals and their welfare, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work in partnership with peers to identify types of animals from audio recordings,
2. compose sentences describing the position of an object in relation to another with words such as next to, under, in front of, between, behind, on, in, beside, outside,
3. role play placing objects at different positions according to instructions given,
4. work closely with peers to identify prepositions from the passages,
5. answer comprehension questions,
6. listen to a resource person on imaginative stories on animals and their welfare, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner engages actively when role playing placing objects at

different positions according to instructions given.

• Learning to Learn: This is promoted as the learner builds on their learning experiences when listening to a resource person

on imaginative stories on animals and their welfare.

Values:
• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner accommodates diverse opinions when working closely with peers to identify

prepositions from the passages.

• Unity: This is shown as the learner cooperates with peers to identify types of animals from audio recordings.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Animal welfare: This is promoted as the learner is exposed to the importance of taking care of the animals.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of prepositions to their learning in Kiswahili.
